gaps: No Korean food at all — a cuisine the wok and kid-friendly palates are perfectly suited for.
No seafood of any kind in 13 mains.
No North African or Maghrebi cuisine.
No Sichuan or Taiwanese Chinese cooking despite owning a carbon steel wok.
Only one North Indian dish (rice kanji); no slow-cooked Punjabi/restaurant-style lentil dishes.
Pork appears once (birria uses beef, blanket dumplings use pork) but no standalone pork project for the Big Green Egg or oven.

ideas.title: Easy Japchae (Korean Stir-Fried Glass Noodles and Vegetables)
ideas.why: Opens Korean cuisine for the first time and is a natural wok dish; meat is simply omitted for the vegetarian with no separate pan needed.

ideas.title: Three Cup Tofu
ideas.why: Introduces Taiwanese cooking and a bold wok-based tofu technique that is as-written vegetarian and unfamiliar to the household.

ideas.title: Mapo Tofu (The Real Deal)
ideas.why: Fills the Sichuan gap and exercises the wok properly; pork is a small garnish that is easily left out for the vegetarian using the site's linked vegan version.

ideas.title: Dal Makhani (Restaurant-Style)
ideas.why: Expands the thin North Indian slot beyond kanji with a slow-cooked black lentil project that is as-written vegetarian and suits the Dutch oven.

ideas.title: Moroccan Fish Tagine
ideas.why: Adds both seafood and North African cuisine — two gaps in one — using the Dutch oven and a tested chermoula technique from ATK.

ideas.title: Char Siu (Chinese BBQ Pork), Restaurant-Style
ideas.why: A Big Green Egg weekend project that fills the Cantonese gap and gives pork a proper starring role; skinless pork shoulder is called for, fitting the household's no-skin rule.
